title_en: Measures on the Administration of Imported Films

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the spirit of the Notice of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, the State Council, and the Central Military Commission on Stopping the Indiscriminate Screening of Internal Reference Films (dated April 14, 1980), for the purpose of strengthening the administration of imported films.

Article 2 The business of importing films for distribution or test screening (including 35mm, 16mm, super 8mm, video tapes, video discs, etc., hereinafter collectively referred to as "films") from foreign countries and the Hong Kong and Macao regions shall be uniformly operated and managed by the China Film Distribution and Exhibition Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the "China Film Corporation").
When a film is imported, Customs shall check and release it against the import goods declaration form filled in by the China Film Corporation. A commercial film to be distributed nationwide shall undergo tax payment procedures at the time of import; a non-commercial film shall be exempted from tax; a non-commercial film that, after import, is approved for nationwide distribution, the China Film Corporation shall, in accordance with the relevant regulations, go through the procedures for supplementary tax payment with the Beijing Customs.

Article 3 Reference films imported by the China Film Archive (including films purchased, exchanged, donated, or acquired by other means as reference materials between the China Film Archive and foreign film archives) are non-commercial films. Customs shall check and release them duty-free against the import goods declaration form filled in by the Archive.
If an imported reference film is approved for nationwide distribution, the China Film Corporation shall, in accordance with the relevant regulations, go through the procedures for supplementary tax payment with the Beijing Customs.

Article 4 Where specialized documentary, scientific, and educational films are imported by entities such as science and technology, industry, agriculture, education, health, press, foreign trade, and foreign affairs authorities for their business needs, if the importing entity is under the system of the State Council, the import shall be approved by the relevant ministry, commission, or bureau (or general administration) under the State Council; if the importing entity is a local entity, the import shall be approved by the people's government of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
When the film is imported, Customs shall check and release it duty-free against the approval document of the relevant ministry, commission, or bureau (or general administration) or the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and the import goods declaration form in triplicate filled in by the applicant entity. Customs shall also forward one copy of the declaration form, bearing the Customs seal, to the Film Administration Bureau of the Ministry of Culture for record.

Article 5 Where feature films are shipped into China by organizations or individuals from foreign countries, the Hong Kong and Macao regions, or Taiwan Province to entities such as government organs, organizations, or schools, if the receiving entity is under the system of the State Council, the import shall be subject to the approval of the Film Administration Bureau of the Ministry of Culture; if the receiving entity is a local entity, the import shall be subject to the approval of the cultural bureau (or film bureau) of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and a copy shall be submitted to the Film Administration Bureau of the Ministry of Culture for record.
When the film is imported, Customs shall check and release it duty-free against the import goods declaration form and the approval document filled in by the receiving entity.
The receiving entity shall hand over the received films to the China Film Archive for unified custody. If special business needs arise, the receiving entity may, with the approval document from its superior competent authority, retrieve the films from the Archive for reference by relevant personnel, but the films shall not be lent out, screened for entertainment, or publicly shown in society. After reference, they shall still be returned to the China Film Archive for custody.
If an imported feature film is approved for nationwide distribution, the China Film Corporation shall go through the procedures for supplementary tax payment with Customs.

Article 6 For scientific and educational films mailed or brought into the country by foreigners, overseas Chinese, and compatriots from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan Province, which are gifted to individuals in China for business reference, Customs shall permit import and shall, upon the import goods declaration form filled in by the recipient individual and a certificate letter from the recipient's unit, check and release them duty-free. Feature films gifted to individuals in China shall generally not be permitted import, and Customs shall return them. In special circumstances, the matter shall be studied and handled by the Ministry of Culture and the General Administration of Customs.
Films carried (or mailed from abroad) by personnel of foreign embassies or consulates in China, permanent representatives of foreign industrial and commercial enterprises stationed in China (including foreign permanent correspondents), and foreign experts recruited to work in China (including cultural, educational, economic, and technological experts) shall be handled in accordance with the current relevant Customs regulations. After import, the films shall be strictly controlled by the relevant authorities and shall be screened only internally by such persons; no Chinese entity or individual shall borrow or screen them.

Article 7 Except for film production in the mainland by the three Hong Kong companies—Great Wall, Phoenix, and Sun Luen—which shall be directly coordinated by the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council with the relevant regions and entities, all coproduction business between China and foreign countries, or between China and the Hong Kong and Macao regions or Taiwan Province, shall be managed by the China Film Coproduction Corporation. The import of co-produced films shall be handled by the China Film Coproduction Corporation for import declaration procedures with Customs. Where such films are approved for nationwide distribution, the China Film Corporation shall, in accordance with the relevant regulations, go through the procedures for supplementary tax payment with the Beijing Customs.

Article 8 Films imported in violation of regulations or smuggled into the country shall be dealt with by Customs in accordance with the relevant provisions. For confiscated films that have preservative or reference value, they may be transferred to the Film Administration Bureau of the Ministry of Culture and handed over to the China Film Archive for preservation.
Article 9 These Measures shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
